stages.title: Arrival task
body: What do you say first when a customer complains?
What does confirm mean?
A drink is spilt on a customer. What do you do?
Why should we avoid arguing about a complaint?
BLUE / GREEN / AMBER / RED. Choose a pause or quiet station.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause, quiet breathing or a quieter station without requiring a public colour disclosure. Agree one return action privately. Expected: listen and apologise; check details are right; pause, keep clear and tell the adult, following agreed safety procedures; arguing blocks a calm solution. The spill is a spoken fictional prompt, not an enacted spill. Individual stations. An adult is the customer and observer. No pair work, cold calling or performance in front of the class. Adults may read, rephrase or scribe the learner’s exact words; they record the help and do not choose the learner’s assessed lines, decisions or tips. A model, blank form or planned duration is not completed individual evidence. These are paper-based training role plays. Do not prepare or serve real food or drinks, make a real booking, take payment or use personal customer details. Use the fictional guest codes and practice dates only. An allergy question means pause the order and ask the responsible adult to check the approved allergen information; never guess or promise a food is safe. A spill is discussed only: pause, keep clear and alert the adult. Follow the setting’s agreed safety procedures for any real incident.

stages.title: The drink is cold
body: A customer says: The drink is cold.
What do you say first?
Choose: apologise / explain / ignore.
Tell the adult why your first step helps.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Adult reads the customer line calmly. Apologise is the supplied best first choice; listen to the issue before explaining or seeking an agreed fix. Do not require shouting, confrontation or emotional escalation.

stages.title: Today I can
body: Take part in four customer role plays and produce three top tips for good customer service.

stages.title: My three top tips
body: Write three tips for good customer service.
You may choose three useful tips from six.
Say why each tip helps a customer.
Use one thing that happened in your role play.
stages.notes: 6 minutes. Completes the source 18-minute You Do. VOC3-L2-E2 records three learner-authored or selected tips and reasons. In the six-choice route, suitable choices are A, C and E. The learner gives the reason in their own way. Aspire explains one tip with a specific observed role-play example; do not invent the example. Adults may scribe exact words.

route_tasks.Supported: Choose three tips from six, then give or dictate your own reason for each.
route_tasks.Independent: Write your own three tips and explain why they help.
route_tasks.Aspire: Explain a tip using a specific example from your role play.

stages.title: Tidy and file
body: Keep your two order tickets, booking form and observation.
File your three top tips card.
Record the support you used.
One thing I improved was __.
stages.notes: 4 minutes. File VOC3-L2-E1 and E2 using the evidence app under the approved workflow. Record actual date, active minutes, individual contribution and support only after the activity. Keep the script and draft corrections if useful. No evidence reference, performance tick or completion decision is pre-filled.

stages.title: Exit ticket
body: Say one top tip.
Explain why it helps a customer.
My tip is __ because __.
stages.notes: 2 minutes. Private adult check, pointing, speech, signing or an agreed supported response. Use a reason linked to the customer, such as repeat-back lets them correct the order. Identify one next step from the actual work.

stages.title: Key words
body: Greet: welcome politely.
Order: what the customer asks to buy.
Booking: arrange a room or service.
Confirm: check the details are right.
Complaint: a report that something is wrong.
Apologise: say you are sorry.
Refer: ask a person who can help.
stages.notes: Untimed reference. Use a concrete line or action to support each meaning. Colour is not the only cue; the situation words and numbers identify the resources.

planner_sections.heading: Purpose and source
paragraphs: Exact outcome: Take part in four customer role plays and produce three top tips for good customer service. Source: Medium Term Plan!D8; Lesson register!F11. Autumn 2 Week 3 Mission. No teaching date is inferred.

The learner works at an individual station with an adult customer and observer: greeting, drink order, room booking and complaint. The order situation includes two tickets. The learner then produces three top tips.

planner_sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Arrival 4; starter 2; I Do 5; We Do 5; You Do 18, split role plays 12 and tips 6; tidy/file 4; exit 2. Total 40 minutes. Opening, outcome, vocabulary and hidden staff slides are untimed.

Aim for about three minutes per situation in the practice block. If the learner needs longer or a pause, record only the actual completed situations and a next step; do not invent completion to fit the plan.

planner_sections.heading: Before the lesson
paragraphs: Prepare the learner’s script, training menu, four calm adult customer cards, two blank order tickets, blank booking form, four-row observation record and tips card with the six-choice support version. Agree the quiet station, communication method and pause/return action.

These are paper-based training role plays. Do not prepare or serve real food or drinks, make a real booking, take payment or use personal customer details. Use the fictional guest codes and practice dates only. An allergy question means pause the order and ask the responsible adult to check the approved allergen information; never guess or promise a food is safe. A spill is discussed only: pause, keep clear and alert the adult. Follow the setting’s agreed safety procedures for any real incident.

planner_sections.heading: Modelling and observation
paragraphs: Model the full complaint with listening, apology, an agreed fix and referral. Then model a booking on the form using fictional Guest A, arrival 14 June, two nights. The assessed card uses Guest C, arrival 18 July, two nights so copying the model cannot supply the actual details.

Agree what the adult will see or hear: polite greeting; two accurate repeat-backs; guest code/date/nights checked; a calm complaint response with a permitted next step. Do not assess accent, eye contact or theatrical performance. Record words, action, corrections and support.

planner_sections.heading: Role cards and answers
paragraphs: Greeting card: customer is new. Accept a polite welcome and offer of help. Order ticket 1: Guest A, one tea and one water. Ticket 2: Guest B, two apple juices and one orange juice. Give one order at a time and confirm after repeat-back.

Booking card: fictional Guest C, arrival 18 July, two nights. Complaint: the drink is cold. Accept listening, apology, a check of what went wrong, a fix within permission or asking the responsible adult to authorise it. Never require a learner to argue or endure an escalating customer.

planner_sections.heading: Routes and learner ownership
paragraphs: Supported keeps the script in hand. Independent attempts without a script. Both use the same outcome with the support recorded. MCQ tips access chooses three from six and gives reasons. Aspire explains a tip using an actual role-play example.

VOC3-L2-E1 is the observed four-situation performance with two tickets and one booking form. VOC3-L2-E2 is the learner’s three top tips and reasons. A completed blank form or a copied tips model is not evidence of independent performance.

Adults may read, rephrase or scribe the learner’s exact words; they record the help and do not choose the learner’s assessed lines, decisions or tips. A model, blank form or planned duration is not completed individual evidence.

Lesson register!I11 selects Teamwork, Coping with Problems, Use of English and Learning. These align with the combined MTP weekly skills. The adult customer provides the interpersonal context; do not force peer pair work or add unplanned Maths or IT skill ticks.

This lesson has 40 planned hospitality minutes; the whole pair has 80 planned minutes in the challenge map. Record actual active minutes, date, contribution, support, evidence reference and observer initials after teaching. Keep Careers time separate. File genuine work and observations in the evidence app.

staff_answers: Greeting: accept a polite welcome, offer of help and time to listen. Communication method may be speech, signing, a script or agreed support; record it. Eye contact or acting style is not the outcome.

Order ticket 1: fictional Guest A, one tea and one water. Order ticket 2: fictional Guest B, two apple juices and one orange juice. Repeat each item and amount; wait for confirmation and correct any error.
Training booking: fictional Guest C, arrival 18 July, two nights. Record and repeat all three details. No real booking, payment or personal data is involved.
Complaint: listen, apologise, check the issue, offer an agreed next step and refer to the responsible adult as needed. Do not argue, blame the customer or promise an unapproved refund or replacement.

Suitable six-choice tips are A, C and E. Their reasons: repeat-back catches errors; polite listening helps the customer explain; an agreed fix/referral gets suitable help. B, D and F need correcting. Learner-authored tips are valid if suitable and explained.

Allergy or spill prompts are spoken fictional scenarios only. Allergy query: pause and ask the responsible adult to check approved allergen information, without guessing or promising safety. Spill: pause, keep clear and alert the adult; follow the setting’s agreed procedures for a real incident.

Record each role actually performed, the learner’s words/actions, support and correction. A blank observation sheet, copied script, model ticket or planned 40 minutes is not completed or earned evidence.

source_clarifications.resolution: Use the register per lesson: Theory plans Learning, Use of English and Teamwork; Mission also plans Coping with Problems. The weekly MTP list describes the combined pair. These are opportunities requiring actual evidence, not automatic ticks. No Maths or IT tick is added.
source_clarifications.status: Recorded source reconciliation; exact outcomes unchanged.

source_clarifications.issue: Realistic customer situations without real service or personal data
source_clarifications.resolution: Use calm paper-based role plays with the adult at an individual station. Guest A/B/C and all practice check-in dates are explicitly fictional training details. No real food, drinks, booking, payment or personal account is used. Allergy and spill prompts are verbal scenarios; pause and refer to the responsible adult.
source_clarifications.status: Classroom implementation of source safety and access prompts.

source_clarifications.resolution: Retain the mapped activity and evidence shape, but leave actual completion, assessor judgement, date, active minutes and records blank until the learner performs the work and it is reviewed.

slides.title: My three top tips
body: Write three tips for good customer service.
You may choose three useful tips from six.

slides.title: Exit ticket
body: Say one top tip.
Explain why it helps a customer.
My tip is __ because __.
slides.notes: 2 minutes. Private adult check, pointing, speech, signing or an agreed supported response. Use a reason linked to the customer, such as repeat-back lets them correct the order. Identify one next step from the actual work.

slides.title: Key words
body: Greet: welcome politely.
Order: what the customer asks to buy.
Booking: arrange a room or service.
Confirm: check the details are right.
Complaint: a report that something is wrong.
Apologise: say you are sorry.
Refer: ask a person who can help.
slides.notes: Untimed reference. Use a concrete line or action to support each meaning. Colour is not the only cue; the situation words and numbers identify the resources.

planner_sections.heading: Purpose and source
paragraphs: Exact outcome: Take part in four customer role plays and produce three top tips for good customer service. Source: Medium Term Plan!D8; Lesson register!F11. Autumn 2 Week 3 Mission. No teaching date is inferred.

The learner works at an individual station with an adult customer and observer: greeting, drink order, room booking and complaint. The order situation includes two tickets. The learner then produces three top tips.

planner_sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Arrival 4; starter 2; I Do 5; We Do 5; You Do 18, split role plays 12 and tips 6; tidy/file 4; exit 2. Total 40 minutes. Opening, outcome, vocabulary and hidden staff slides are untimed.

Aim for about three minutes per situation in the practice block. If the learner needs longer or a pause, record only the actual completed situations and a next step; do not invent completion to fit the plan.

planner_sections.heading: Before the lesson
paragraphs: Prepare the learner’s script, training menu, four calm adult customer cards, two blank order tickets, blank booking form, four-row observation record and tips card with the six-choice support version. Agree the quiet station, communication method and pause/return action.

These are paper-based training role plays. Do not prepare or serve real food or drinks, make a real booking, take payment or use personal customer details. Use the fictional guest codes and practice dates only. An allergy question means pause the order and ask the responsible adult to check the approved allergen information; never guess or promise a food is safe. A spill is discussed only: pause, keep clear and alert the adult. Follow the setting’s agreed safety procedures for any real incident.

planner_sections.heading: Modelling and observation
paragraphs: Model the full complaint with listening, apology, an agreed fix and referral. Then model a booking on the form using fictional Guest A, arrival 14 June, two nights. The assessed card uses Guest C, arrival 18 July, two nights so copying the model cannot supply the actual details.

Agree what the adult will see or hear: polite greeting; two accurate repeat-backs; guest code/date/nights checked; a calm complaint response with a permitted next step. Do not assess accent, eye contact or theatrical performance. Record words, action, corrections and support.

planner_sections.heading: Role cards and answers
paragraphs: Greeting card: customer is new. Accept a polite welcome and offer of help. Order ticket 1: Guest A, one tea and one water. Ticket 2: Guest B, two apple juices and one orange juice. Give one order at a time and confirm after repeat-back.

Booking card: fictional Guest C, arrival 18 July, two nights. Complaint: the drink is cold. Accept listening, apology, a check of what went wrong, a fix within permission or asking the responsible adult to authorise it. Never require a learner to argue or endure an escalating customer.

planner_sections.heading: Routes and learner ownership
paragraphs: Supported keeps the script in hand. Independent attempts without a script. Both use the same outcome with the support recorded. MCQ tips access chooses three from six and gives reasons. Aspire explains a tip using an actual role-play example.

VOC3-L2-E1 is the observed four-situation performance with two tickets and one booking form. VOC3-L2-E2 is the learner’s three top tips and reasons. A completed blank form or a copied tips model is not evidence of independent performance.

planner_sections.heading: Regulation and learner voice
paragraphs: BLUE low energy; GREEN ready; AMBER tense; RED overwhelmed. Offer a brief pause, quiet breathing or a quieter station without requiring a public colour disclosure. Agree one return action privately.

Individual stations. An adult is the customer and observer. No pair work, cold calling or performance in front of the class. Adults may read, rephrase or scribe the learner’s exact words; they record the help and do not choose the learner’s assessed lines, decisions or tips. A model, blank form or planned duration is not completed individual evidence.
